knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Attribute access default fallback loss in graph tracing
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Tracing and code transformation frameworks may not preserve fallback semantics for attribute access, causing generated graphs to diverge from original behavior.

risk_dimensions.shape: Default fallback values with shape-like semantics (e.g., torch.Size) may not survive tracing.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Default fallback values of various dtypes (int, Tensor, None) may be lost or coerced incorrectly.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Original and traced module execution may diverge when fallback values are used for missing attributes.

failure_mechanism.description: During symbolic tracing, the framework converts Python operations into graph nodes. When encountering getattr with a default fallback, the transformation may drop the fallback value, causing the traced graph to raise an exception or produce incorrect results when the target attribute is missing.

input_exploration: Explore modules whose forward methods use getattr with default fallback values for missing attributes
Vary the target attribute name, including existing, non-existent, and dynamically generated names
Vary default fallback value types such as shapes, integers, tuples, tensors, and None
Run both original and traced modules on representative inputs to compare behavior
constraint_awareness: Tracing frameworks may not support all Python builtins with fallback semantics
Default values must be exactly preserved in the traced graph
Attribute targets may be absent at trace time or execution time
oracle_strategy: Compare outputs of original and traced modules for inputs that rely on default fallback
Monitor for exceptions or crashes during symbolic tracing or traced module execution

transferability.reason: Any code transformation or tracing framework that converts Python code into a graph risks dropping dynamic fallback semantics for attribute access. This principle applies beyond torch.fx to other symbolic tracing, JIT compilation, or graph extraction tools.

important_considerations: Focus on attribute access with fallback defaults rather than only direct getattr usage
Ensure that traced and original modules are executed under identical conditions
Consider fallback values that have structural or type significance (e.g., shapes, device, dtype)
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that create modules with varied getattr fallback patterns and compare original vs traced execution, rather than reproducing the specific missing attribute case.
